question: A conductor is connected to a battery of 2V. Let V₁ be the potential difference across the conductor. When a battery of 4V is connected, the potential difference becomes V₂. The ratio(V₁/V₂) is:
solution:
The correct answer is 'large{1over 2}'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

 
• Ohm's law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.

V = IR 

 
• Where V is the voltage difference, I is current passes through conductor and R is the resistance.
 
• A conductor is connected to a battery of 2V. Let V1 be the potential difference across the conductor, then

 V₁ = IR = 2 ...(1)

 
• When a battery of 4V is connected, the potential difference becomes V2.

V₂ = I2 R = 4....(2)

 
• Divede equation (1) by equation (2) .

 [IMAGE: data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw==] [IMAGE: data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAPABAP///wAAACH5BAEKAAAALAAAAAABAAEAAAICRAEAOw==] 

large{V1over V2} = {IRover I2R} ={2over 4} = {1over 2}
